name: why-bldc-ceiling-fans-cost-more
title: Why BLDC ceiling fans cost more, and when they pay off
summary: A plain guide to BLDC fans and two models on sale now.

body.p: BLDC is a type of motor. Fans built with one use much less electricity than regular ceiling fans, but they cost more to buy. Whether that is worth it depends on how many hours a day the fan runs. A regular fan running ten hours a day can use more than twice the power of a BLDC fan doing the same work. Most BLDC fans sell for somewhere between ₹2,500 and ₹4,500, while a basic regular fan can cost under ₹1,500. In a bedroom or living room where the fan stays on through the night, the saving on the bill usually covers that gap within two summers. In a guest room, or for a fan used only on the hottest afternoons, it can take many years, and the cheaper fan makes more sense.
If a fan runs most of the day, the lower power use adds up. For a room used now and then, a regular fan is often the better buy.
Check that the blade size suits your room before you order.
